name: Daiki Kumakura
profile: I am a mathematical biologist and a bioinformatics researcher in the pharmaceutical industry. I received my Ph.D. in Life Science from Hokkaido University in March 2025.
expertise: My expertise is in mathematical modeling and quantitative data analysis. I work on how dynamic systems can be represented, what can be learned from observations, and how assumptions affect the conclusions. My current interests include pharmacometrics and model-informed drug development.

career.text: Bioinformatics researcher in the pharmaceutical industry

education.text: Ph.D. in Life Science, Graduate School of Life Science, Hokkaido University
Master’s degree, Graduate School of Life Science, Hokkaido University
Bachelor’s degree in Fisheries Science, Department of Aquaculture Life Science, School of Fisheries Sciences, Hokkaido University

research_background.title: Mathematical modeling
research_background.body: Dynamical systems and differential equations, with an emphasis on models that capture the essential structure of a problem. I use models to connect mechanisms with observed patterns and to examine competing explanations.

research_background.title: Statistical inference and uncertainty
research_background.body: Parameter estimation, time-series analysis and model evaluation. I focus on what the available data can support, where uncertainty remains, and how conclusions depend on modeling assumptions.

research_background.title: Interactions and causal reasoning
research_background.body: Analysis of interactions in dynamic systems, including CCM (Convergent Cross Mapping). I am interested in distinguishing predictive relationships from causal interpretations and making the assumptions behind each analysis explicit.
